original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a finite set P of points in the plane whose visibility graph is exactly G, where two points of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of P.
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, Open Problem 1: Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a set of points in the plane. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct problem type (recognition of point visibility graphs), the paper's input model (a graph given in adjacency-matrix form), the ambient setting (points in the plane), and the paper's visibility rule based on whether the joining segment contains or passes through any other point of the set. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: The paper treats this specifically as a decision problem: determine whether the given graph is a visibility graph, not a broader characterization or reconstruction task. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

A fully stand-alone formulation should make explicit the one-to-one correspondence between the vertices of G and the points of P that is implicit in the definition of a visibility graph. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

It should specify that P is a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane and that no general-position assumption is imposed; collinearities and blockers are allowed in the model. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
It should preserve the exact input representation from the paper: a finite graph presented in adjacency-matrix form. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
There are no additional paper-critical algebraic parameters here such as field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers; the only missing precision is geometric/combinatorial.
refined_question: Given a finite graph G in adjacency-matrix form, decide whether there exists a finite set P ⊂ R^2 and a bijection φ:V(G)→P such that for every two distinct vertices u,v ∈ V(G), uv ∈ E(G) if and only if the line segment joining φ(u) and φ(v) does not contain or pass through any other point of P. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
equivalent_formulation: Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form, determine whether G is a point visibility graph, i.e., the visibility graph of some set of points in the plane. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: The draft clearly targets the point-visibility recognition problem from Section 2.1 rather than a neighboring coloring or clique question. In the introduction, the paper defines mutual visibility for a point set P in the plane and defines the visibility graph by assigning one vertex to each point and connecting two vertices exactly when the corresponding points are mutually visible. Section 2.1 then says that asking whether some point set has a given graph as its visibility graph is the visibility graph recognition problem and states Open Problem 1 in essentially the same terms as your draft. No extra restrictions such as integer coordinates, prescribed reconstruction, or general position appear in the statement. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
